intent.raw: Create a research strategy so we understand what domainspec-lean-formalization is about, uncover its methods, research direction, insights, and relation with other repositories inside the root; use fan out, zig-zag, and dialectics, and identify what else we can get alongside those lanes.
intent.objective: Design a governed, evidence-cited research route for understanding domainspec-lean-formalization as a Lean theorem/research repository, its methods, its direction, its insight surface, and its relations to DomainSpec, Arcanum, CyberAlchemy, project snapshots, and sibling root repositories.
intent.operator_sentence: First recover the repo's own claim/proof guardrails, then fan out into bounded research lanes, zig-zag each lane through critique, run a dialectic over competing readings, and synthesize a path-cited map plus next-route handoff without promoting claims past evidence.

route_menu.context_hint: The route is read-only research. It can recommend delegated lanes, but execution requires operator approval.

items.label: Fanout + critique + synthesis
items.description: Parallel lanes map different evidence surfaces, then each lane is critiqued before a parent synthesis.

items.label: Single reader x-ray
items.description: One agent maps the repo sequentially; cheaper but more likely to miss cross-register tensions.

items.label: Robot talks audit
items.description: Use role-bound critique to find tensions among theorem claims, operational framing, and repo relations.

items.label: Task session report
items.description: Execute the approved route as a bounded work pack that produces the research brief and evidence ledgers.

technique_overlays.trigger: domainspec-lean-formalization explicitly requires claim text to remain a subset of Lean proof, theorem, audit, or literature evidence.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Every insight or relation claim is either path-cited as evidence, demoted to hypothesis, or moved into the residue ledger.

technique_overlays.trigger: The target asks for relation with other repositories inside the root, which crosses owner and authority boundaries.
technique_overlays.validation_expectation: Relations are recorded as evidence-backed links, analogies, candidate dependencies, or open questions; none become canonical ontology without owner review.

subagent_strategy.trigger: The repository mixes Lean proofs, mathematical prose, research bridges, operational Arcanum relations, internal tools, and cross-repository lineage.
subagent_strategy.explanation: A mixed fan-out catches independent evidence surfaces quickly, while the zig-zag and dialectic phases prevent one attractive narrative from outrunning proof or relation evidence.
context: domainspec-lean-formalization/CLAUDE.md says the repo is an atlas of residue and enforces claim <= proof.
README.md frames the repository as DomainSpec Theorem, with Lean development, research spine, bridges, and Mathlib PR-ready files.
LEAN-ARCHITECTURE.md maps ten Lean clusters and names Bicyclic, ResidueStructure, F11, SignalNoiseDecomposition, ReflectionTower, and M6Counter as load-bearing.
docs/spine-cyberalchemy-relation.md says the mathematical spine and CyberAlchemy are the same framework in formal and operational registers.
ops/development/lean-formalization-skill-agent-candidate-ledger.md already separated Lean proof/governance surfaces from generic DomainSpec skills.

roles.purpose: Map Lean files, clusters, proof/build status claims, sorry/build obligations, Mathlib PR-ready files, and load-bearing definitions.
Extract the research thesis, methods, two-layer/three-axis model, open conjectures, and documented direction from README, research spine, docs, backlog, and audits.
Map relations to Arcanum, CyberAlchemy, implementation/domainspec, root projects, and sibling repositories without overclaiming equivalence.
Challenge novelty, proof strength, analogy strength, and publication-bound claims; classify claims as proved, refuted, conjectural, analogy, or unsupported.
Turn lane receipts into a usable brief with method map, insight ledger, relation graph, next questions, and route recommendations.

subagent_strategy.permission_prompt: Run five bounded research roles over domainspec-lean-formalization to produce a path-cited research brief, relation graph, claim ledger, and next-route handoff?
receipt_requirements: Each role returns concrete path evidence for every material claim.
Each role classifies claims by evidence status: proved, build-evidenced, documented, conjectural, analogy, refuted, or unsupported.
Each role records tensions and rejected readings in the residue ledger.
No role promotes findings into Inventory, Ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell surfaces.

steps.name: Recover local router, prior ledger, and claim/proof guardrails
stop_conditions: Block any write or publication-bound summary that claims novelty without precedent/audit evidence.
Flag any claim that exceeds Lean proof, build evidence, documented audit, or cited literature status.
Keep the route read-only unless the operator separately approves execution artifacts.

steps.name: X-ray the repository as artifact system
stop_conditions: Flag surfaces that are historical, generated, scratch, or PR-staging rather than core theorem evidence.
Do not collapse Lean files, prose essays, research bridges, internal tools, and operational docs into one evidence class.

steps.name: Fan out into method, proof, direction, insight, and relation lanes
convergence_criteria: Method lane identifies formal method, proof method, counterexample method, bridge method, and audit method.
Proof lane separates sorry-free claims, stated build targets, open obligations, Mathlib PR-ready candidates, and scratch/historical files.
Research direction lane extracts current thesis, open problems, planned tracks, and demoted/refuted claims.

Relation lane classifies links to arcanum, cyberAlchemy, implementation/domainspec, projects/*, and root sibling repositories as direct dependency, shared vocabulary, imported snapshot, analogy, candidate relation, or unrelated.
All lane receipts include concrete path evidence and residue.
stop_conditions: Block if lanes cannot provide path-cited evidence.
Flag any lane that treats analogy as theorem or proof as operational readiness.

steps.name: Map relations to DomainSpec root surfaces and sibling repositories
convergence_criteria: Each relation has source path, target path, relation type, evidence confidence, and open question.
Internal domainspec-core relations are separated from sibling checkout relations under /home/vrondelli/projects.
Operational Arcanum/CyberAlchemy relations are not promoted into mathematical equivalence without explicit proof or cited synthesis.
stop_conditions: Block mutation of sibling repositories.
Flag relation claims based only on name similarity.

steps.name: Zig-zag lane claims through critique and demotion
convergence_criteria: Every strong claim is either backed by cited proof/build/audit evidence or demoted.
Every contradiction is assigned to proof gap, literature gap, relation gap, stale artifact, or genuine tension.
The loop stops after two critique passes or when no claim status changes.
stop_conditions: Stop after two advocate/critic turns per lane.
Block publication-bound novelty claims without literature or precedent evidence.

steps.name: Run a dialectic over competing interpretations and select a bounded reading
convergence_criteria: Winning interpretation explains Lean corpus, research spine, bridges, operational relations, and PR staging without flattening them.
Rejected interpretations are preserved with what they explain well and what they distort.
The selected reading is small enough to become the first paragraph of the research brief and rich enough to recompose into the relation graph.
stop_conditions: Flag if no interpretation can explain both formal Lean and operational Arcanum/CyberAlchemy relations.
Choose a bounded reading instead of forcing total unification.

steps.name: Synthesize the research brief and alongside artifacts
stop_conditions: Include methods, research direction, insights, relation map, claim-status table, open questions, and recommended next routes.
Do not write canonical ontology/glossary/inventory promotions from the brief.

steps.name: Validate evidence coverage and promotion guardrails
stop_conditions: Block if the final brief contains uncited strong claims.
Flag if any relation lacks a confidence status or owner boundary.
Flag if proof/build status is inferred without checking the relevant file, README status, or build evidence.

steps.name: Handoff next route options
stop_conditions: Next execution requires explicit operator approval.
Memory visibility updates and canonical artifact promotion remain separate decisions.

gates.condition: This dispatch designs the strategy and may produce read-only research artifacts only; no repository mutation beyond approved strategy artifacts.
Narrative claims must be a subset of Lean proof, build evidence, documented audit, or cited literature; otherwise they are demoted or recorded as residue.
Every relation to another repository or root surface must carry evidence path, relation type, confidence, and owner boundary.
Recommended fan-out/subagent execution requires explicit user approval before delegated runtime work starts.
Execution evidence and research receipts summarize findings only and do not promote inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell artifacts.

boundaries.contract: Import path-cited evidence and summaries only; do not edit theorem, proof, research, or router files.
Relations to sibling repositories are evidence-backed observations or hypotheses, not authority transfer or ontology promotion.
Delegated lanes return receipts with artifacts, validation result, audit references, and residue; parent synthesis owns interpretation.

authority.validation: dispatch-spec validator plus skeptical-math-auditor claim checks
authority.evidence: path-cited repository artifacts and lane receipts
authority.memory: memory visibility only after separate user request

promotion_splits.target: inventory, ontology, glossary, sigil, and spell artifacts
promotion_splits.rule: Evidence may be summarized as handoff input only; canonical promotion requires owner review and separate approval.
Memory updates, if requested later, do not imply canonical knowledge promotion.

promotion_guardrails: The route does not claim promotion authority for Inventory, Ontology, glossary, sigil, or spell artifacts.
The route does not claim mathematical novelty without cited precedent/audit evidence.
The route does not treat Arcanum/CyberAlchemy relation synthesis as formal equivalence unless a cited proof/audit supports that stronger claim.
The route keeps proof/build/PR mechanics inside dedicated Lean capability surfaces rather than generic DomainSpec workflow.
